issues: Broken Markdown structure: original includes extra top-level headings '# BAB I...  ' and '# BAB II...  ' before '# BAB I' and '# BAB II', but these are missing in the translation.
Scrambled/merged list structure in Article 2 and Article 3: list items 'a.' and 'b.' are run together on the same line (and 'and/orc.' is merged), which can break downstream list-boundary parsing.

Leftover non-legal placeholder text carried over: '13. Perlindungan...' and '24. Keluarga...' appear as '13. Protection...' and '24. Family...' in the translation; these are not substantive provisions and should be removed (the actual definitions already follow as item 13 and 24).

Scrambled/altered list-marker structure in Article 3(2): original has inline markers "a.", "b.", and "dan/atau c." without a separate line break between "dan/atau" and "c."; translation reformats into a nested list, changing marker structure used for downstream splitting.

Minor meaning drift in Article 1(6): Indonesian "baik fisik, seksual, ekonomi, sosial, psikis" means "whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological" (types of suffering), but the translation reads awkwardly as if addressed "to the victim"; corrected to clearly modify "misery or suffering".

Scrambled/merged list structure: several lettered items run together on the same line (e.g., Article 5 b/c; h/i/j/k; Article 7(1) and 7(2) introductory text merged with item a; Article 14(1) c/d and Article 14(3) intro merged with item a).

List marker/content mismatch and duplication artifacts retained (e.g., "obtain...  g.", "make...  c.", "psychosocial...  c.", "monitor...  f.") need to be preserved but correctly positioned as in the original.
Meaning drift: Article 5(d) mistranslates "peradilan di luar pengadilan" as "courts outside the judiciary"; should be "out-of-court dispute resolution"/"non-judicial settlement".
Meaning drift: Article 7(5) translates "APBD" as "Regional Budget"; should be "Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget (APBD)" to preserve the legal term.

Scrambled/incorrect list structure in Article 5: items b–k are not consistently kept as list items (some run as plain paragraphs) and the original has b and c on the same line; ensure each marker a.–k. appears once in order as list items.

Scrambled/incorrect list structure in Article 7(1) and 7(2): in the original, the lettered subitems a–d and a–c are attached directly after 'dalam bentuk:'; translation reformats them as an indented sublist, which can break downstream boundary matching.

Scrambled/incorrect list structure in Article 12(c): original has 'c. pelayanan...  c. pelayanan psikososial'; translation renders 'c. psychosocial...' which changes the meaning of the ellipsis fragment (it should be 'services...' not 'psychosocial...').

Scrambled/incorrect list structure in Article 14(1): original has 'c. Advokat; dand. Pekerja Sosial.' (no line break between 'dan' and 'd.'); translation inserts 'and' on its own line, altering marker adjacency.

Scrambled/merged list structure: several sub-items (a.–e. in Article 15; a.–b. in Article 17; a.–h. in Article 18) are run together with the preceding text (missing line breaks after ':'), which can break downstream list-boundary parsing.
Leftover ellipsis text carried over from the source: "Supervision..." in Article 16 and "to summon..." in Article 18 are not legal text and should be removed.

Meaning drift in Article 20(3): Indonesian says the offense in paragraph (1) is a violation; translation says "criminal act" (singular) and omits that it is specifically the offense in paragraph (1) (should be "The offense ...").

Broken/scrambled list structure: in the original Article 16 contains a duplicated item number "3." (one as an ellipsis "Pengawasan..." and then the full supervision clause). The translation collapses this into a single item 3, so the list markers do not match the source structure.
Meaning/structure omission tied to numbering: the standalone "3. Pengawasan..." line in Article 16 is missing in the translation.
Meaning drift: "Huruf b...AngkaalS" contains OCR/garbled text; translation leaves it as-is instead of rendering it as an ellipsis/continuation marker ("..."), which can mislead downstream evaluation.
Minor meaning drift: "AngkaalS" is not part of the legal content and should not appear in the English legal text.
